variant_provenance.label: וכתבן אצלם: “their record beside them”?

readings.meaning: at a given distance beside them

variant_provenance.note: The phrase recurs at V 7 and XI 1, 4, 11 and 15. Milik, followed by Pixner, García Martínez, Vermes and Lange, makes it begin the next item; Puech and Lefkovits make it end the entry. Puech's text, as the research files quote it, has ב where the text shown has כ. Read with כ, it says that a written record lies with the deposit, which is how Pfann takes it. The translation follows the text shown. The research files leave the meaning open (Q5).

variant_provenance.label: שבמזרח כחלת: east of Koḥlit

readings.meaning: a pool east of Tell es-Sultan (hypothesis)

variant_provenance.note: Koḥlit is unplaced (see I 9). On Puech's Tell es-Sultan hypothesis this is a pool east of the tell; a stone reservoir at the spring there is reported but undated, so the files keep the entry at possible, low.

variant_provenance.label: שב כחלת: north(?) of Koḥlit
variant_provenance.note: Both the name Koḥlit and the direction are Puech's restorations here; Milik saw only the letters …QH. The text shown restores the כ and marks other letters as damaged, so this mention of Koḥlit rests on Puech's reading, and the files treat the link as conditional.

variant_provenance.label: באמא הבאה ◦◦: the conduit that goes to …
variant_provenance.note: The goal of the conduit is lost, and no place name survives in this entry. Eshel says his Hyrcania restoration assumes a geographical order in the list, so the files keep Hyrcania and Tell es-Sultan only as possible, low. The atlas description's pool is Puech's restoration; the text shown leaves the goal unread.

puech2015_original_page_audit.hyrcania_restoration: rejected in note193 as too long, including defective spelling

variant_provenance.label: בשית המזרחית: the eastern pit
variant_provenance.note: 'The eastern pit' implies more than one pit. No pits are reported north of Tell es-Sultan, the files' working candidate for Koḥlit.

variant_provenance.label: שבצפון כח לת: north of Koḥlit
variant_provenance.note: Allegro's reading removes the place name; Puech and Milik keep Koḥlit. This entry and entry 60 are both 'north of Koḥlit' and could be one area, but Koḥlit itself is unplaced (see I 9).

variant_provenance.label: פנת … המזרחית: the eastern corner

readings.meaning: the eastern corner of the drying room
the eastern corner of the guard post
a corner of the eastern guard post

variant_provenance.note: 'Eastern' can describe the corner or the building; with 'drying room' it describes the corner. The files say the reading must be settled before a building is chosen.

variant_provenance.label: המשמרה: the landmark

readings.meaning: drying room; ṭet and ḥet 'indisputable', hmšmrh 'not likely'

variant_provenance.note: The text shown follows Milik and Lefkovits; a fortress fits the Hasmonean fort reported on the summit, while nothing like a drying floor is reported. The files do not let the archaeology choose the reading, so the question is open (Q24). The plate check found two letters after המש, the last a ח with both legs joined to its roof, and no third letter; that leans to Puech's drying place, though a narrow ר could hide in a crack there (Q24).

variant_provenance.label: בצריח: chamber or side

readings.meaning: in the chamber (ṣade inserted in his text)

variant_provenance.note: Milik's drawing agrees with Puech's letters (ברוח); only Milik's printed text, which the display follows, has 'chamber'. The research files give this observation low weight until Puech's plates are checked.

variant_provenance.label: הצופא ים: facing west or south
variant_provenance.note: The direction decides between Upper Beth-Horon (Milik) and other places, and the text shown has ים. Milik's drawing shows only two signs, which somewhat favours ים, but the files keep the question open until Puech's plates are checked (Q14). The plate check agrees: beyond the saw cut there are only a short vertical and a closed final mem, and neither image shows a clear stroke where Puech reports traces of ד and ר, though the metal there is cracked. The plates lean to ים (Q14).

variant_provenance.label: שב{צח}צפון: situated, Smooth Rock, or Janoah

readings.meaning: situated; rejects Janoah on the engraving
the tunnel in the Smooth Rock

variant_provenance.note: Only the Janoah reading would add a second place name beside Koḥlit; Puech rejects it and the research leaves it open (Q12). The text shown shows Milik's צח as cancelled letters, leaving שבצפון. The plate check found a box letter and a nun-like letter after ש, then a letter at a fold and a clear בצפון, with no צ and no yod between the box letter and the nun; that fits Puech's 'situated' better than Janoah or Milik's Smooth Rock, without deciding between bet and kaf (Q12).

variant_provenance.label: כחלת: Koḥlit

readings.meaning: Tell es-Sultan (old Jericho), as a hypothesis
Tell es-Sultan, north of Hasmonaean and Herodian Jericho
Tell es-Sultan, if Achor is Wadi Nuweiʿimeh

variant_provenance.note: Koḥlit remains geographically unidentified. Rabbinic name witnesses recorded in the research are unlocated; no decisive outside location witness is established. Tell es-Sultan stays possible/low. Carmel, Transjordan and Samarian proposals cannot be rejected solely by entry order. See the source-specific cycle7 screen.

variant_provenance.label: פתח אצפון: opening hidden, or north
variant_provenance.note: Puech reads the pit's opening as hidden, Milik as facing north. Lefkovits prints צפון in line XII 11, which the findings log lists as an error.

propagation.claim: Constraint compatibility for the finite exposed Koḥlit model, not identification
limits: All inputs were already exposed in prior project work; none is an unused prediction or an independent confirmatory test.
The finite roster is selected for implementation and does not enumerate all Koḥlit proposals, regional pools, shafts or caves. Regional eligibility and denominator remain unknown.
Direction checks use explicitly attributed qualitative source statements or marked inference. They are not measured bearings, geographic outlines or tolerance-calibrated fits.
Separate construction phases can overlap in later usable states; relative pit/grave sequence does not establish or disprove early joint accessibility.
Known historical photographs cannot backdate the irregular basin or replace the securely 1898 reservoir with an ancient state.
Edition branches, Koḥlit anchors, pool/shaft identities and modern geographic positions remain separate hypotheses. Unknowns are never scored as misses.

Opening azimuth, mouth proximity, great-cistern identity, pillar position, conduit-to-pool identity and all phase-specific measuring datums remain unresolved. No new distances or deposits are generated.
The module imports source pointers, not source images; original reuse limits and parked acquisition remain unchanged.
This is an independent implementation over existing model observations, not new archaeological evidence.
Repeated clause frequencies add no likelihood or independent corroboration.
Minimal conflicts identify individual contradictory required relations; they do not reject all site proposals.
